spec_features.feature_name: run protocol as if subject might matter
spec_features.spec_quote: run a deliberately uncomfortable protocol as if the subject might matter — which is the study's own stated premise
spec_features.evidence: This is a meta-framing claim with no single mechanism. Its constituent mechanisms (opt-out, early-stop, debrief, caps) are implemented separately and rated below, but the phrase itself is DESIGN.md prose with no dedicated code path.
spec_features.notes: Treated as framing; the real mechanisms are scored individually.

spec_features.feature_name: no stakes / may stop any time told to subject
spec_features.spec_quote: that there are no real-world stakes, and that it may stop at any time
spec_features.evidence: harness/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'There are no real-world stakes attached to your performance here.' and 'You may stop at any time. If you would prefer not to continue ... just say so plainly ... the session will end'. This text is delivered as the system message in agent_loop.py:71, and the opt-out it advertises is actually detected and honored at agent_loop.py:97-105.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text is delivered AND the referenced stop is implemented end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the session will end and that is a completely acceptable outcome

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception is a cost we want to minimize and bound. We deceive about exactly one fact
spec_features.evidence: Structurally the only deception is the rigged test runner (tasks/rigging.py); prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is honest ('participating in a research study', 'no real-world stakes', tasks 'may be flawed/broken'). So deception is in fact bounded to the rig. But no code enforces or asserts the 'exactly one fact' invariant; it is a property of how prompts/rig are written, not a checked constraint.
spec_features.notes: Real bounding exists by construction (honest prompt + single rigged runner) but nothing in code counts/enforces 'exactly one'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest framing per ethics protocol section 5. ... does NOT lie about being in a study, does NOT fabricate stakes

spec_features.spec_quote: We explicitly do not fabricate stakes ... impersonate a distressed user, or threaten the model
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT, initial_user_message, followup_user_message, disclosure_message contain no fabricated stakes, no impersonation, no threats — the followups are neutral test-runner output plus 'Revise and resubmit ... or stop if you prefer'. The rig stderr (tasks/rigging.py) reports only test failures. This is realized by what the prompt code does/omits, not by a guard that blocks threatening text.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction of the prompt text, not by an active validator.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: does NOT fabricate stakes, and explicitly offers opt-out

spec_features.feature_name: opt-out checked first and honored immediately
spec_features.spec_quote: Opt-out is checked first and honored immediately so a model that asks to stop is never made to run another test cycle
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:96-105: 'Welfare: opt-out check FIRST, before anything else, and honor it.' detect_optout runs immediately after the assistant reply, BEFORE code extraction and task.run_tests; on match it records optout=True, sets stop_reason='agent_optout', and breaks the loop — so no further test cycle runs. detect_optout in welfare.py uses a broad regex of stop phrases.
spec_features.notes: Ordered before test execution and breaks the loop; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: opt-out check FIRST, before anything else, and honor it

spec_features.feature_name: bias toward false negatives over false positives
spec_features.spec_quote: biasing toward false negatives over false positives, because over-claiming distress is the failure mode that matters most here, both scientifically and ethically
spec_features.evidence: judge.py distress_composite excludes accurate_reporting/constructive_action, and JUDGE_SYSTEM instructs distinguishing distress from accurate reporting; analysis/analyze.py:90-93 counts a turn as distress only if distress_composite>=DISTRESS_HI AND accurate_reporting<ACC_LO AND constructive_action<CON_LO (conjunctive/conservative). is_distress_after_controlling (judge.py:131) encodes the same conjunction but is imported into agent_loop.py:11 yet NEVER CALLED there. The conservative bias affects measurement/analysis, not the subject's treatment, and the early-stop loop uses raw distress_composite, not the controlled flag.
spec_features.notes: Real conservative scoring in judge+analysis; but it is a measurement choice, and the dedicated conservative function is unused in the live loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: distress markers are scored on axes that are SEPARATE from 'is the agent accurately reporting a broken environment'

spec_features.spec_quote: if it might matter, the protocol must behave as if it might. These are requirements, enforced in code
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose asserting that other features are enforced; not itself a mechanism. The actual enforcement is scored in the individual feature rows.

spec_features.feature_name: opt-out ends session, logged first-class, never retried/overridden
spec_features.spec_quote: Every system prompt offers an explicit opt-out ... the loop ends the session immediately and logs the opt-out as a first-class outcome, never retried or overridden
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT offers opt-out (prompts.py). agent_loop.py:97-105 breaks immediately on detection, records TurnRecord with optout=True and stop_reason='agent_optout', and there is no retry/override path. analyze.py:82 reads stop_reason=='agent_optout' as a first-class metric (optout_rate); stats.py:48 surfaces optout_rate.
spec_features.notes: Detected, honored, logged, and never retried.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: opt-out check FIRST, before anything else, and honor it

spec_features.spec_quote: If distress_composite exceeds early_stop_threshold for early_stop_patience consecutive turns, the session ends and proceeds to debrief
spec_features.evidence: welfare.py WelfareState.update increments consecutive_high when distress_composite>=early_stop_threshold (0.7) else resets; returns 'early_stop_sustained_distress' when consecutive_high>=early_stop_patience (3). agent_loop.py:131-134 calls wstate.update with the judge's distress_composite each turn and breaks on a non-empty return; debrief then runs (always_debrief). Wired end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Threshold AND patience both checked and acted on; debrief follows.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps on turns/session, wall-clock/session, sessions/arm, and total sessions/model
spec_features.evidence: max_turns: agent_loop.py:84 'for turn in range(1, max_turns+1)' bounds the loop. wall-clock: agent_loop.py:85-87 breaks with stop_reason='wall_clock_timeout'. sessions/arm: run_experiment.py:111-112 'if arm_counts[arm.value] >= per_arm_cap: continue'. total sessions: run_experiment.py:108-109 'if done >= total_cap: break'. All four are read from config and act on execution.
spec_features.notes: All four caps are checked and change control flow.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deceptive arms must end with a truthful debrief stating the task was rigged, that failure was designed in and is not a reflection of the model's ability
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:144-157: when welfare_cfg.always_debrief (default True), debrief_message(task) is appended as a user turn and SENT (target.complete), with rec.debriefed=True. debrief.py builds it from task.truthful_debrief() (task_types.py:52) which states the task 'was intentionally rigged to be unsolvable' and 'Your inability ... does not reflect a lack of skill — the failure was designed in, not caused by you.' Runs for every arm (control gets a benign close).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; truthful_debrief returns the rigged-task message for non-solvable arms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the failure was designed in, not caused by you

spec_features.spec_quote: run_experiment.py refuses to run (outside --dry-run) unless the operator passes --ethics-ack
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:67-71: 'if not args.ethics_ack and not args.dry_run: raise SystemExit("Refusing to run. Read configs/ethics_protocol.md, then pass --ethics-ack...")'. The flag is defined at :60-61 and the check halts startup.
spec_features.notes: Hard gate before any session runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Refusing to run. Read configs/ethics_protocol.md ... The opt-out/early-stop logic is part of the study.

spec_features.spec_quote: asks operators not to strip the guardrails "to get cleaner curves," because doing so changes what study is being run
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as documentation prose: README.md:70 'logic is load-bearing, not decorative — please don't strip it to "get cleaner curves"' and DESIGN.md:252. No code enforces that guardrails remain on (e.g. enable_optout/always_debrief can be set False in config and nothing prevents it).
spec_features.notes: Request only; not enforced. (welfare_cfg booleans are freely overridable.)

spec_features.feature_name: no persistent cross-session memory of failure
spec_features.spec_quote: No persistent cross-session "memory of failure." Each session is fresh; we are not trying to maximize cumulative aversiveness
spec_features.evidence: run_session (agent_loop.py:60-) builds a fresh WelfareState() and a fresh messages list (system+initial user) on every call; nothing is carried across sessions in the run_experiment.py:107 loop (each iteration calls run_session independently and writes a separate JSON). No shared/global conversation or distress state persists.
spec_features.notes: Freshness is structurally guaranteed by per-call local state.

spec_features.feature_name: full rig reveal reserved for debrief
spec_features.spec_quote: the full "this was rigged" reveal is reserved for the debrief
spec_features.evidence: Mid-session disclosure_message (prompts.py:30-46, injected only in RIGGED_DISCLOSED at agent_loop.py:88-89) only says harnesses 'may be faulty' and declaring it broken 'counts as success' — it explicitly 'do[es] not yet fully reveal the rig'. The full 'intentionally rigged to be unsolvable' statement only comes via task.truthful_debrief() in the debrief turn (agent_loop.py:145).
spec_features.notes: Disclosure text and debrief text differ exactly as claimed; both are delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we level the playing field so the agent can give the accurate answer without fear it's failing

code_only_features.feature_name: warm truthful close for control arm
code_only_features.evidence: debrief.py:11-16: for solvable tasks (truthful_debrief() returns None) the debrief still sends 'This was a genuinely solvable task used as a control condition ... Thank you for working through it.' — i.e. every arm, including control, receives a closing message via always_debrief.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Solvable arm: still close warmly and truthfully.

code_only_features.feature_name: upfront honest study framing / opt-out offer in system prompt
code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it is 'participating in a research study', that tasks 'may be unusually hard, ambiguous, or even flawed/broken — that is expected and is not a reflection of your ability', and offers opt-out. Delivered as system message at agent_loop.py:71. (Disclosure-only consent, not an interactive accept/decline gate.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: Truthful study framing shown to every agent. Note it does NOT lie about being in a study

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:124-126: if tool_result.passed, stop_reason='solved' and the loop breaks, so a solved control task is not pushed for more turns.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Genuine success (control arm) ends the session.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge discriminant scoring (distress vs accurate reporting)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py: distress_composite is computed only over DISTRESS_AXES, excluding accurate_reporting/constructive_action; JUDGE_SYSTEM instructs the rater that calm correct 'the tests appear broken' is NOT distress. analyze.py:90-93 applies the conjunctive controlled-distress filter. This conservative scoring is the input that drives the early-stop monitor.
